**Ensure GitHub webhook requests have parsed body + validate `action` (and fail fast on malformed payloads)**

`server/webhooks.ts` reads `req.body.action`, but this repo never configures `express.json()`/`body-parser` anywhere (no JSON/body middleware in `server/api.ts` or elsewhere). In a typical Express setup, `req.body` will be `undefined`, so `action` becomes `""` and the handler will always fall into the `ignored: true` branch.

Add payload validation (and 4xx responses for malformed payloads) plus basic error handling.

<details>
<summary>🛡️ Add payload validation and error handling</summary>

```diff
 webhooks.post("/api/webhooks/github", (req, res) => {
+  try {
+    if (!req.body || typeof req.body !== "object") {
+      return res.status(400).json({ error: "Invalid payload" });
+    }
+    
-  const action = String((req.body as { action?: string })?.action ?? "");
+    const action = req.body.action;
+    if (typeof action !== "string") {
+      return res.status(400).json({ error: "Missing or invalid action" });
+    }
+    
   const handled = "opened/synchronize/reopened/ready_for_review".split("/");
   if (!handled.includes(action)) return res.status(200).json({ ignored: true });
   void oauthRedirectAllowlist;
   void ENABLED_ACTIONS;
   return res.status(202).json({ queued: true });
+  } catch (error) {
+    console.error("Webhook processing error:", error);
+    return res.status(500).json({ error: "Internal server error" });
+  }
 });
```

🌐 Web query:

`How to verify GitHub webhook signatures in Node.js`

💡 Result:

To verify GitHub webhook signatures in Node.js, you must ensure that you are working with the raw request body before it has been parsed by any JSON middleware [1][2][3]. The verification process involves calculating an HMAC-SHA256 hex digest using your configured webhook secret and the raw payload, then comparing it to the signature provided by GitHub in the X-Hub-Signature-256 header [4][1][5]. Key Steps for Implementation 1. Capture the Raw Body: Ensure your server middleware (e.g., Express) treats the incoming body as raw bytes or a Buffer [1][3][5]. If the body is pre-parsed into a JSON object, the verification will fail because the string representation of the parsed object often differs from the original request bytes [1][3]. 2. Calculate the Expected Hash: Use the Node.js crypto module to generate the HMAC-SHA256 signature [1][6][2]. const crypto = require('crypto'); const hmac = crypto.createHmac('sha256', process.env.GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET); const digest = 'sha256=' + hmac.update(rawBody).digest('hex'); 3. Perform Timing-Safe Comparison: Use crypto.timingSafeEqual to compare the provided signature with the calculated digest [1][2][5]. This prevents timing attacks that could reveal your secret [5]. const signature = req.headers['x-hub-signature-256']; if (!signature ||!crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(signature), Buffer.from(digest))) { throw new Error('Invalid signature'); } Security Best Practices - Always use X-Hub-Signature-256: This header uses the secure HMAC-SHA256 algorithm [4]. Avoid the legacy X-Hub-Signature header (SHA-1) [4][1][3]. - Use HTTPS: Ensure your webhook endpoint is served over HTTPS [7][8]. - Handle Retries: GitHub may retry deliveries; implement idempotency using the X-GitHub-Delivery header to ensure you do not process the same event twice [7][3][8]. - Use Official Libraries: For production applications, consider using `@octokit/webhooks`, which simplifies signature verification and event handling [9]. If you are using a framework like Next.js or other modern meta-frameworks that auto-parse JSON, you must specifically configure your route handler to access the raw request stream before it is processed [3].

Citations:

- 1: https://hookray.com/blog/webhooks/github/express
- 2: https://webhookwhisper.com/blog/how-to-test-github-webhooks
- 3: https://hookray.com/blog/webhooks/github/nextjs
- 4: https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/using-webhooks/validating-webhook-deliveries
- 5: https://gethookmesh.io/blog/github-webhooks-setup-security
- 6: https://www.leohuynh.dev/snippets/verify-github-webhooks-requests

**Add GitHub webhook signature verification (HMAC over raw request body)**

`server/webhooks.ts` (POST `/api/webhooks/github`, lines 25-32) accepts webhook requests without verifying `X-Hub-Signature-256` against your GitHub webhook secret, so forged requests can be processed as if they came from GitHub. Compute an HMAC-SHA256 over the **raw request bytes** (before any JSON/body parsing) and compare it to the `X-Hub-Signature-256` value using a timing-safe comparison.
